Clause-②: **no** — ⛔ the lookup contract does **not** change. Only the failure message gains a suggestion.

**File surface:** the OBJUI-001 "Unknown component type" failure path, and `objectui check`'s equivalent output, plus tests and a changeset.

⚠️⚠️ **HARD SERIAL FENCE — read before your first edit.** **#5373 is in flight right now** retiring `CRUDSchema`, and it holds `packages/core/src/validation/schema-validator.ts`, `packages/core/src/builder/schema-builder.ts`, `packages/cli/src/__tests__/check-known-types.test.ts`, `packages/types/src/crud.ts`, `packages/types/src/zod/crud.zod.ts` and `packages/types/src/index.ts`. ⛔ **If your edit needs any of those exact files, stop and report** — do not race it. The suggestion belongs in the registry-lookup-miss path and in the CLI's suggestion-emitting code, which should be different files; ✅ say in your report which files you actually needed. Other siblings: #5729 (`plugin-grid`), #5969 (`plugin-detail/src/renderers/`), #5420 (app-shell designer save→publish), #5852 (`packages/types`, landing).

## 裁决 — the maintainer RULED this. ⛔ Do not re-open it.

⚠️ The card is titled `[Decision]`, but **the decision has been made.** Maintainer ruling recorded 2026-08-19 (27-card decision-inbox review, maintainer's verbatim reply 「全部接受」):

> **Ruling: Option C — keep lookup strict, make the failure teach.**
> - Registry lookup **stays case-sensitive**; when a lookup misses **and a case-insensitive match exists**, the OBJUI-001 "Unknown component type" panel **and** `objectui check` both add the suggestion: `Unknown component type 'Page' — did you mean 'page'?`
> - **Option A (do nothing) is rejected** — it does nothing about recurrence of a silent whole-page failure.
> - **Option B (normalise at lookup) is rejected** — a permanent stack-wide contract change (docs, designer, `sdui-intrinsics.d.ts`, every registration site) that also **legalises the typo class** (`PAGE`, `pAge`), paying a contract cost for tolerance C can simply name.
> - Both measured instances were our own artifacts fixed at source, so the pull justifies **teaching, not tolerating.**

⛔ **Do not normalise the lookup.** ⛔ Do not add a case-insensitive fallback that resolves the component. The lookup must still **miss**; only the **message** changes. ⚠️ If you find yourself making `'Page'` render, you have implemented rejected option B.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, do not inherit

1. ⚠️ **Two surfaces, and they must agree.** The ruling names **both** the OBJUI-001 panel and `objectui check`. ⛔ Doing one is half the card. ✅ If they cannot share the suggestion logic, say why rather than writing it twice — and if a shared helper is the answer, prefer reaching an existing export over minting a new published one (that would be Clause-②, and you should ⛔ stop and report instead).
2. ⚠️ **"A case-insensitive match exists" needs the live registry, not a retyped list.** Read the candidate set from the registry itself. ⛔ A suggestion built against a hand-maintained copy of the type list goes stale silently and will confidently suggest a type that no longer exists. (#5115 / PR #5128 already made the CLI derive its `knownTypes` from the registry for exactly this reason — reuse that, do not re-fork it.)
3. ⚠️ **Say nothing when there is no match.** `Unknown component type 'zzz'` must **not** acquire a bogus "did you mean". ✅ Pin the no-match case as its own leg, in the same run as the match case.
4. ⚠️ **Case-insensitivity is the ruled trigger — ⛔ not fuzzy distance.** `'Page'` → `'page'` is in scope. `'pge'` → `'page'` is **not**, and adding it would be scope the ruling did not grant. ⛔ Do not reach for a Levenshtein helper.
5. ⚠️ **Check what the panel does today before adding to it.** The OBJUI-001 message may already be assembled in more than one place (a renderer fallback and an error-formatting helper). ✅ Find the real emit point with a counter-probe and report it; ⛔ do not add a second message producer.

## Verification

Predict the direction **before** running. The load-bearing pin is a mounted render with `type: 'Page'` where `'page'` is registered: ✅ the node **still fails** (⛔ it does **not** render — that is the rejected option B), **and** the message carries `did you mean 'page'`. Both halves in one assertion set, plus the no-match counter-probe from item 3 in the same run.

⚠️ **Three phantom-class defects and one phantom *instrument* were self-caught by devs on this round's cards**, all one root: *an assertion or control that cannot distinguish the two states of the world.* ✅ State explicitly **which of your assertions would still pass if your change were reverted**, re-aim any that would, and make each control a string present in **both** versions of the file.

⚠️ **Commit your own edit before you ablate** — measured on #5859 today: a `trap` restore using `git checkout --` reverted the dev's still-uncommitted edit along with the probe's mutation, and it **reported success both times**.

⚠️ **A cached turbo green is not a measurement** — measured on #5852 today: an un-forced sweep reported **77/78 cached**, indistinguishable from a build that never looked. Use `--force` on any turbo-run gate you are treating as evidence, and say so.

Prove every mutation on disk by grepping injected **and separately** removed text; ⚠️ print the landing site; ⚠️ assert anchor uniqueness before writing; ⚠️ restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with a **cwd-independent** command; confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` is empty afterwards.

**Gates by name, with exit codes:** `type-check` for every package you touch (⚠️ hyphenated; echo the script name; distinguish the **unbuilt-closure** red — `Cannot find module @object-ui/...` — from the **missing-`node_modules`** red; ⚠️ **build `./examples/**` too**, not just `./packages/**` — that gap turned a sweep red on #5876 today and was environmental, not a finding), root-form vitest quoting per-test names, the downstream **prefix-form** sweep with the direction **demonstrated** rather than asserted, eslint with merge-base delta (⚠️ plain `eslint .`; ⛔ no `--no-inline-config`).

⚠️ **Use `pnpm exec vitest run [paths]` from the repo root** — ⛔ **not** `pnpm --filter … test -- [paths]`, which **silently drops everything after `--`**; guarded (objectui#3288) and the guard fired on a live PR today. ⚠️ **Zero-match pnpm trap** — caught live twice today: a filter matching nothing prints *"No projects matched the filters"* and exits **0**. Run `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` rather than guessing — ⚠️ **#6073 widened it beyond `/src/`** today. Changeset **`patch`** (a message improves; no type moves). ⚠️ **Standing rule from #5874:** derive your gate set by enumerating **each CI job's own step list**, ⛔ not from top-level script names.

## Deliverable

Draft PR, body with `Fixes #5247`. ⛔ Do not mark ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ no auto-merge — the PM lands it. Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker `os-dev-report`; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders in prose — this repo's sanitizer eats them, confirmed repeatedly today) and return it. State, per gate: command, exit code, what a red would have meant; which files you needed and whether any collided with #5373's fence; the real emit point for each of the two surfaces; **which of your assertions would still pass on a revert**; and any deviation with its reason.

## PM rulings on the two flagged deviations — **both stand. ⛔ No rework.**

### 1. The quoting differs per surface — **correct, keep it**

The panel emits `— did you mean 'page'?` and the CLI emits `— did you mean "page"?`. You asked whether the ruling's single-quote spelling is meant literally on the CLI too.

⛔ **It is not.** The ruling's `Unknown component type 'Page' — did you mean 'page'?` is an **illustration of the clause**, not a byte specification — its own words are *"both **add the suggestion**"*. ✅ And each surface following its own existing convention is the better outcome: the CLI warning already spells the offending type as `"Page"`, so a single-quoted suggestion on that line would have been the only single-quoted thing in a double-quoted sentence. **A line that disagrees with itself is worse than two lines that differ from each other**, and the clause wording is identical on both sides, which is what "one spelling" was protecting.

### 2. Appending rather than replacing — **correct, keep it**

`Unknown component type: Page — did you mean …` keeps the colon and the bolded type that existing tests and docs pin. ✅ Same reasoning: the ruling says *add*, and replacing the sentence would have broken pins for a cosmetic match to an illustrative string.

---

## The Clause-② stop was self-applied, and the reasoning is why I am not asking for convergence

The dispatch said the two surfaces must agree and that if they cannot share the logic you should **say why rather than write it twice**. ✅ You did, and the measurement settles it:

> The published CLI runs inside a user's project and depends on **neither `@object-ui/core` nor the plugin packages that register most component types** — `scripts/regenerate-known-schema-types.mjs`'s own header records that **eleven of the fifteen** real types in the old hand list are registered by packages the CLI does not depend on, so a runtime registry lookup **would answer the wrong question there**.

⇒ The only module both could import is `@object-ui/react`, and putting a helper in its public surface **mints a new published export** — Clause-②, which the dispatch told you to stop and report on rather than do. ✅ **Two short unexported helpers, cross-referenced in both headers, with the emitted wording pinned behaviourally on both sides** is the right answer, and it is right *because the candidate sets genuinely differ*, not as a convenience.

⚠️ And each side reads from the set it can actually trust — the renderer from the live `ComponentRegistry.getKnownTypes()` (loaded registrations **plus pending lazy stubs**, which is the lazy-registration trap #6014 measured today), the CLI from the registration-derived `KNOWN_SCHEMA_TYPES` snapshot from #5115/PR #5128, **reused rather than re-forked**. That is assumption 2 answered exactly.

## The emit point was established by counter-probe, and it found something

⭐ Mutating `ERROR_CODES['OBJUI-001'].message` left the panel **byte-identical** — that template is **dead for the panel** (`createError('OBJUI-001', …)` has no call site outside `packages/core/src/errors/__tests__/errors.test.ts`) — while mutating `.suggestion` **did** reach it. ✅ So there is exactly **one** message producer and this change adds to it rather than creating a second, which is what assumption 5 was for. ⛔ And `plugin-report`'s own "Unknown component type" string was correctly identified as a **plugin-local fallback on a different path** and left alone.

## The phantom instrument, self-caught — sixth this round, and a new species again

⚠️ **Leg 3's first run reported its verdict from a `console.log` that vitest never surfaced**, so it printed *"marker did NOT reach the panel"* in the **unmutated baseline too** — the same answer in both states of the world. ✅ Replaced by a probe **writing the panel text to disk**, gated on a baseline self-check for a control string present in both versions; only then were the legs believed.

✅ And a first ablation attempt was **rejected by its own on-disk proof**: the "removed text" check failed because the mutation only **inserted** a line rather than removing one. Rewritten with single-line anchors so **both halves of the proof were real**. That is the disk-proof rule doing exactly what it exists for — refusing a mutation that was never two-sided.

## The revert answer is the best this round

> *Stated because half of them do, deliberately.*

✅ **Survive a revert** — the `RENDERED_MARKER` absence check, the `role=alert` panel presence, "still contains Unknown component type", "Page is still reported unknown", both `not.toContain('did you mean')` legs, and the `pge` legs. And the reason each survives is given: the first group is the **anti-option-B guard** (without it, a future change could satisfy every suggestion assertion by simply **accepting** the mis-cased type — which is the rejected option), and the second is the **counter-probe against a clause that fires unconditionally**, meaningless alone and therefore pinned in the **same run** as a positive case.

✅ **Fail on a revert** — the 2 renderer and 3 CLI "did you mean" cases, **demonstrated red by ablations 1 and 2 rather than claimed**. Plus one more that pins the *candidate-set choice itself*: the renderer test **unregisters `page` mid-test** and asserts the suggestion disappears, which is what makes the candidate set demonstrably the **registry's own** rather than a snapshot.

## Two more things read correctly

⚠️ The forced turbo downstream sweep was **killed by the container's ~10-minute foreground cap** (SIGTERM, exit 124) at 64/68 with **zero failures**, and was completed in the cache-free `pnpm … run type-check` form — **33 projects, 32 real `tsc` invocations, no turbo cache in the path at all**. ✅ That is a *stronger* measurement than the forced turbo run would have given, and saying so beats reporting a timeout as a gap. (It also compounds today's #5852 lesson: a cached green is not a measurement.)

✅ **End-to-end on the BUILT binary**, not just source: a tmpdir with a `Page` file and a `zzz` file produced exactly the two expected lines. A suggestion feature verified only in-process would not have proved the published CLI does it.

✅ **No collision with #5373's fence**, and the one adjacency was named rather than glossed: #5373 holds `check-known-types.test.ts`, which exercises the `check.ts` line edited here — that test was **not modified** and passes in the 40-file blast-radius sweep.
